correctness.rationale: For every tree n>=3, edge differences form the dual of the fundamental centered-cut basis, and W is its L1 norm. A direction with >=2 active edge differences lies in a positive linear sign chamber of a sphere of dimension >=1, so cannot minimize there. Each 1-edge direction has strictly positive sharp tangent coefficient because distinct cut covariances satisfy |Kef|<Kee. The projected cut basis and triangle inequality prove the exact attained tangent minimum. A uniform bound |d_e(z)|<=sqrt(2) makes the geodesic formula exact below the stated tangent threshold. Path/star specializations follow by exact Gram substitution. The standalone Fraction checker reproduced 1,440 exhaustive small labeled trees, 56,262 tangent mixtures, and the specialized identities.

originality.rationale: The principal claim is the complete all-tree local width-minimum landscape and attained finite-angle profile, not the already-known global minimum width. The published graphical zonotope source deals with deformation cones; broad Rayleigh-quotient and graph-total-variation sources describe flows or L1 normalization; an indexed global inradius result controls only global cut minima. None of their verified statements logically determines the sharp coefficient gamma_e or path-star factor n-2. Priority against inaccessible longer writings remains provisional.

value.rationale: A natural complete optimization landscape is computed for an infinite class of geometric objects: exactly 2(n-1) strict wells and the attained local geodesic width function about each. This is not merely the known global Cheeger/inradius value. Quantified stability is meaningful because n-vertex star and path zonotopes have equal width at their leaf-edge wells yet angular slopes differing by n-2, a diverging structural separation at fixed dimension. The precise invariant is directly motivated by robustness of local directional-width minima.
